jurisdiction.service_area_note: Applies across the national jurisdiction; Riyadh and Jeddah are display cities of the same schedule.
jurisdiction.note: The case the model was migrated for. One schedule, two display cities, tariff logic held once.

grade_reason: Grade B and unpriced. Two material blockers, neither of them a rate: the VAT treatment of residential usage, sewerage and the meter service charge has not been established from a regulated source, and the reading of the first band rests on a worked example in a state press release rather than on the regulator's annex.

reference_connection.designation: The regulated schedule sets the meter service charge by size band; 0–20 mm is the residential band.

component_states.question: The first-band reading rests on a worked example in a state press release. Under §7.1 a press agency is discovery; the regulator's annex is canonical and has not been captured.
SAR 5/month for 0–20 mm is reported but not captured from the regulated schedule.
The generic 15% Saudi rate must not be applied automatically. Residential usage, sewerage and the meter service charge may be treated differently and each needs a regulated source.
Sewerage is 50% of the corresponding water rate, but whether the reference account is connected is account-dependent.

components.name: Water use
components.rate_display: SAR 0.10/m³ to 15 m³, then 1.00, 3.00, 4.00, 6.00 — pending capture from the regulator's annex

blocking: VAT treatment unresolved for three components separately
the first-band reading rests on a press release rather than the regulator's annex
basket_note: At most one of Riyadh and Jeddah may enter the UWTI basket: freezeBase() refuses more than one territory per country. Both are published as city records when the blockers clear; only one is a constituent.
register_note: If this figure is ever published it will be SAR 6.50 a month before tax, which would be the cheapest bill in the Index by an order of magnitude. Rule 13 forbids calling it cheap or efficient: a low bill measures what the household pays, not what the water costs to produce, and Saudi Arabia is among the most water-scarce countries on earth.
